corrections.after: C2 G2 C3 G3 C3 G2 (six attacks at sextuplet positions)

sections.title: Opening: tonic pattern and first departure
Varied return and approach to the middle
Independent left-hand patterns and chromatic sequence

chunks.label: Pickup–2
chunks.focus: Learn the Eb5 pickup, then the Ab/C/Eb arpeggio. The first bass is Ab1; later bass attacks rise to Ab2. Notice F5 at the start of measure 2.
Learn the G/Db inner pattern in measure 3, then the Bb5-to-Ab5 melody in measure 4. E naturals change both staves halfway through measure 4.
Anchor the low Db2 entry and higher Db3 repetitions. Measure 6 changes its bass on each beat and introduces Cb; name each six-note cell.
Follow the descending upper line into the lower register. Keep the D naturals in measure 7 distinct from the Db material in measure 8.
Rebuild the opening Ab arpeggio as a separate occurrence. Recall the low Ab1 entry rather than assuming every bass is Ab2.
Compare with measures 3–4: the inner pattern returns, but measure 11 now reaches Bb5 and C6 before G5. Measure 12 restores the E naturals.
Compare with measures 5–6. Measure 14 reaches C6 then repeats G5 over a changing F-to-E inner pattern; do not copy measure 6 unchanged.
Learn B, D and E naturals explicitly. The lower D4 is natural in the last two cells of measure 15. All four lower-staff cells in measure 16 have six attacks.
Learn the repeating E2–C3–Bb3–C3 lower pattern independently of the six-note upper cells. The upper melody changes to Db5 on beat 3.
The bass stays F2 while the upper lower-staff tone descends Bb3, Ab3, G3, F3. The upper staff changes C5, D5, E5, F5.
Remember G2–Eb3–Db4–Eb3 below the six-note upper pattern. The upper first note changes to F5 on beat 3.
The Ab2 bass returns. The upper lower-staff tone descends Db4–C4–Bb3–Ab3 while the upper melody rises Eb5–F5–G5–Ab5.
Learn the four changing lower cells separately: Eb2, C3, F2, then G2 entries. The last lower group has five attacks. Watch D and B naturals.
Both staves return to six-note cells. Learn the explicit E, D and B naturals; the last G pitches in both staves are natural, not sharp.
Anchor the B2 bass after the first cell. Learn the G sharps and the low E4/D4 naturals; the lower-staff B3 and D4 are also natural.
Anchor A2. Name C# and F# while keeping the low E4 and D4 natural. The last cell introduces G# in both staves.
Begin with A and E naturals and C#. Rise through the chromatic sequence, then flatten A to Ab in the last cell in both staves.
Alternate low Db2 and Db3 bass entries. The upper line C6–Bb5–Db6–F5 changes its inner pattern halfway through the measure.
Alternate Eb2 and C3 in the bass. Learn the upper Bb5–Ab5–C6–Eb5 outline and the inner-pattern change on beat 3.
Alternate Eb2 and Bb2 below. The upper outline Eb5–E5–F5–Eb5 requires restoring Eb after the natural.
Learn the shorter lower groups around F2/C3 separately. The upper staff descends Db5 to C5 before leaping to C6 in the last cell.
Alternate Bb1 and Bb2. The last two cells flatten F in both staves; do not reuse the unaltered pattern from measure 26.
Relearn the returning measure-27 pattern at this occurrence. Connect its Eb2/C3 bass alternation to the altered pattern in measure 32.
The lower pattern now uses A3 and C4, with F4 at the end. Learn the upper Eb5–F5–Gb5–F5 outline and A naturals.
Name the B and D naturals below. The third upper cell starts on A5 natural and uses B4 natural; keep its F4 inner attack.
The Eb bass supports widening register changes. The third cell has A naturals in two octaves; the last cell leaps to Gb6.
Learn the high F6 entry and the changes from D natural to Db below and F to Fb above. Finish the descent to G5 before returning to Ab.
Reconnect the Ab return to the changing upper line in measure 37: F5, Eb5, C6, G5. Keep every inner arpeggio attack.
The return repeats, but measure 39 reaches F6 rather than the previous C6. Learn this changed summit as its own landmark.
Recall the returning Ab pattern with its F5 change, then descend through the alternating Db5/C5 cells in measure 41.
Learn the low Ab1 accompaniment and alternating Bb4/Ab4 upper cells. Measures 42–43 repeat the same note pattern before the register sweep.
The upper staff begins with a rest, then joins the rising sweep. Read the actual sounding octaves under the ottava marking; both staves change register.
Connect the continuing high-to-low and low-to-high sweeps. Keep the lower staff a distinct sequence; avoid shifting either hand an octave.
After the first descending cell of measure 46, settle into the narrower repeating Ab pattern. Carry it through all of measure 47.
Recall the closing single attacks and rolled chords in any chord-tone order. The D2/Eb2 grace lead-in and trill length are flexible; the main Eb2 and final chord remain required.

ornaments.policy: Optional D2–Eb2 lead-in and any number of D2/Eb2 trill alternations around the required main Eb2. No speed or alternation-count grade.
